# Borrow Service Provider

[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0)

Borrow Service Provider defines the provider contract used by Borrow Kit and
ships the default HTTP implementation for Circle's Borrow Service, covering
loan listing (`getLoans`), partial repayment (`repay`, `getRepayQuote`), loan
position reads (`getPosition`), collateral management (`addCollateral`,
`withdrawCollateral`), reward claiming (`claimRewards`, `getRewards`), and
`registerWebhook`.

`registerWebhook` builds the EIP-712 `WebhookRegistration` typed data,
obtains a signature via the connected adapter, and submits the signed
registration for verification (including EIP-1271 support for smart
contract accounts). This is a permissionless, client-signed flow with no
on-chain transaction and no API key.

Health-band notifications sent to the registered URL are delivered
at-least-once: the same crossing can arrive more than once. Deduplicate on the
notification's `event_id`, which is stable across redeliveries of one crossing.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @circle-fin/provider-borrow-service
# or
yarn add @circle-fin/provider-borrow-service
```

This provider is included by default in `@circle-fin/borrow-kit`. Import it
directly when you need to customize provider construction or compose your own
Borrow Kit context.

## Quick Start

> **Note:** `@circle-fin/borrow-kit` is not yet published — this example
> shows the intended usage once it ships. Until then, construct
> `BorrowServiceProvider` and call `registerWebhook` on it directly with a
> resolved `EVMChainDefinition`; see [Configuration](#configuration) below.

```typescript
import {
  createBorrowKitContext,
  registerWebhook,
} from "@circle-fin/borrow-kit";
import { BorrowServiceProvider } from "@circle-fin/provider-borrow-service";
import { createViemAdapterFromPrivateKey } from "@circle-fin/adapter-viem-v2";

const provider = new BorrowServiceProvider();
const context = createBorrowKitContext({ providers: [provider] });
const privateKey = process.env.PRIVATE_KEY;
if (!privateKey) throw new Error("PRIVATE_KEY is required");
const adapter = createViemAdapterFromPrivateKey({ privateKey });

const result = await registerWebhook(context, {
  from: { adapter, chain: "Arc_Testnet" },
  loanId: "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
  webhookUrl: "https://example.com/webhook",
});

console.log(`Registered webhook: ${result.webhookUrl}`);
```

## Configuration

`BorrowServiceProvider` accepts default configuration in the constructor and
per-operation configuration on each request. Per-operation values take
precedence, while omitted values continue to use constructor defaults.

An API key is optional only for `borrow` and `getBorrowQuote`, and required for
`getIntegratorConfig` and `setIntegratorConfig`. Every other API rejects a
configured key before making a request (or, for `registerWebhook`, before
signing).

```typescript
const provider = new BorrowServiceProvider({
  apiKey: process.env.CIRCLE_API_KEY,
  baseUrl: "https://api-staging.circle.com",
});
```

`apiKey` takes a Circle API key (`<ENV>_API_KEY:<keyId>:<keySecret>`). A legacy
`KIT_KEY:<keyId>:<keySecret>` value goes in the same field and still
authenticates; the console no longer issues them. It is a server-only secret
and is refused in a browser. Omit it for keyless routes.

Calling `registerWebhook` directly on the provider requires a resolved
`EVMChainDefinition` and the connected wallet's address in addition to the
adapter. `EVMChainDefinition` values (such as `ArcTestnet`) currently live in
the internal `@core/chains` package, which is not published standalone — the
snippet below illustrates the shape expected until `@circle-fin/borrow-kit`
(which resolves chains by name, as shown in Quick Start) is published:

```typescript
import { ArcTestnet } from "@core/chains";

const result = await provider.registerWebhook({
  adapter,
  chain: ArcTestnet,
  address: "0x1234567890123456789012345678901234567890",
  loanId: "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
  webhookUrl: "https://example.com/webhook",
  deadline: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 300,
});

console.log(`Registered webhook: ${result.webhookUrl}`);
```

The `BorrowServiceProvider` implements wallet-scoped loan listing through
`GET /v1/borrowKit/loans`, including cursor pagination, response validation,
retry behavior, and structured errors.

It also implements the partial-repayment and full-close prepare/quote
endpoints. Repay requests reuse a caller-provided idempotency key or generate
one when omitted; full-close writes generate one. Quote requests remain
side-effect free and omit it.
